scenes.title: 1965 MIT Neurophysiology Room: Melzack & Wall Testing High-Speed Forearm Touch Buzz Against the Chalkboard Spinal Gate
scenes.era: 1965, MIT neurophysiology laboratory-seminar room, Cambridge, Massachusetts

layout.description: Sunlit 1965 MIT laboratory room featuring a slate chalkboard drawn with the classic four-node Gate Control diagram (Large touch fiber '+', Small ache fiber '-', SG Gate, T output) beside an oak demonstration bench holding a brushed-metal prototype tactile nerve stimulator and thick-vs-thin nerve cable rods.

positions.who: Ronald Melzack (2.5D matte cream-white vinyl adult professor in 1965 herringbone tweed jacket and dark narrow tie)
positions.where: standing beside the slate chalkboard tapping white chalk firmly onto the 'SG' spinal gate junction blocking the 'T' output line

positions.who: Patrick D. Wall (2.5D matte cream-white vinyl neurophysiologist in rolled white Oxford sleeves)
positions.where: seated on the oak bench edge pressing a round tactile buzz pad onto his bare left forearm and turning up the brushed-metal dial
positions.facing: facing the forearm pad and stimulator dial

props.name: prototype brushed-metal forearm tactile nerve stimulator and skin pad
props.period_detail: 1960s low-voltage pulse box wired to round forearm tactile pads recruiting 100 m/s A-beta touch fibers
props.physical_behavior: State-A dial at OFF as pressure gauge pinches forearm -> State-B dial clicked ON sending gentle tactile buzz as tense forearm unclenches

props.name: slate Gate Control chalkboard diagram and thick-vs-thin nerve rod pair
props.period_detail: contrasts the thick insulated 100 m/s touch rod against the thin 2 m/s bare ache wire beside the L/S/SG/T schematic
props.physical_behavior: State-A open chalk gate path -> State-B Melzack drawing bold blocking bar across the T-cell arrow

actions.verb_sequence: presses blunt pressure gauge onto bare forearm -> clicks ON the brushed-metal tactile buzz dial -> rotates wrist smoothly in relief as sharpness vanishes
traces fast Large-fiber chalk arrow into the spinal gate -> draws firm top-down Central Control arrow from brain to spine

reactions.reaction: satisfied nod and relaxed drop of shoulders as 100 m/s touch buzz silences the pinch
confident smile underlining the spinal gate checkpoint

scenes.wardrobe: 1965 MIT academic dress: Melzack in brown herringbone blazer, white shirt, slim dark tie; Wall in crisp rolled white Oxford shirt sleeves and charcoal trousers.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key New England tall-window daylight across slate board and brushed aluminum dial.
scenes.recognition_hook: Buzzing fast touch nerves on his own bare arm at MIT, Patrick Wall proves you can slam a biological gate inside your spine before slow pain signals ever reach your brain!

key_visual.description: two 1965 MIT neuroscientists beside a Gate Control chalkboard schematic testing a brushed-metal tactile nerve-stimulator pad on a bare forearm

scenes.title: Sunlit Outdoor Backyard Patio Bench: Instinctive Bumped-Shin Rub Winning the 100 m/s Nerve Race
scenes.era: Modern sunlit outdoor backyard garden patio

layout.description: Bright open-air brick garden patio in morning sunlight where a 48-year-old adult carrying a watering can bumps a shin against a low cedar patio bench and immediately sits down to rub the shin briskly with both palms.

positions.who: 48-year-old homeowner (2.5D matte cream-white vinyl adult in rolled flannel overshirt and chinos)
positions.where: seated on the sunlit outdoor cedar bench vigorously rubbing above and below the bumped shin with both palms
positions.facing: seated outdoors on sunlit garden patio

props.name: low cedar outdoor patio bench and galvanized garden watering can
props.period_detail: relatable weekend backyard moment triggering the universal shin-rubbing reflex
props.physical_behavior: State-A shin bumps cedar corner (watering can set quickly on patio) -> State-B both palms rubbing shin briskly as grimace melts into calm exhale

actions.verb_sequence: bumps shin on outdoor cedar bench -> sets watering can down and rubs shin briskly with both hands -> stands back up walking smoothly without a limp

reactions.reaction: sharp wince dissolving within three seconds into an easy relieved sigh

scenes.wardrobe: Adult weekend garden attire: rolled plaid overshirt over cotton tee, khaki chinos, canvas sneakers.
scenes.lighting: Warm open morning sunlight across green patio planters and cedar wood.
scenes.recognition_hook: Rubbing a bumped shin on the backyard bench isn't superstition — it fires 100 m/s touch cables to beat 2 m/s ache wires to your spine!

scenes.title: Modern Clinic Chair: Pairing Cool Vibration + Slow Exhale to Close Both Halves of the Gate

layout.description: Clean sunlit outpatient chair where a 55-year-old adult presses a palm-sized cool vibrating pad above the shoulder while exhaling slowly during a routine vaccination.

positions.where: seated with dropped relaxed shoulders looking calmly out the window while holding a small vibrating cool pack near the deltoid
positions.facing: seated calmly in sunlit clinic chair

positions.where: completing a quick routine shoulder band-aid step beside the chair

props.name: palm-sized cool tactile vibration pack
props.period_detail: clinical TENS-descendant buzzer activating fast A-beta fibers alongside calm top-down breathing
props.physical_behavior: State-A held idle in lap -> State-B pressed gently above shoulder as shoulders drop smoothly downward

actions.verb_sequence: presses cool vibrating pad above upper arm -> exhales slowly dropping tense shoulders -> blinks in surprise that the routine shot barely registered

reactions.reaction: pleasantly surprised smile realizing bottom-up buzz + top-down calm shut the gate together

scenes.wardrobe: Short-sleeve navy cotton polo and slacks; clinician in clean teal medical scrubs.
scenes.recognition_hook: Combine local touch vibration with a slow, calm exhale, and you close your spinal pain gate from below and above at the exact same time.
